children.text: The Philippines' signature resort island, famous for its roughly
4km
White Beach and paraw sailboat sunsets. It has grown even cleaner since a major environmental rehabilitation in
, and with direct flights from Korea to Kalibo, it remains a favorite for families and couples alike.
Boracay is a small island off the northwestern tip of Panay Island, part of the municipality of Malay in Aklan province, about
7km
long and less than
1km
wide at its narrowest point. On the island's west side, White Beach stretches for about
4km
of fine, flour-white coral sand, and at dusk, traditional paraw sailboats glide across a red sky, creating the scene travelers around the world remember in photos.

White Beach is divided into Stations 1, 2, and 3, named after the old boat landing points. Station 1 in the north has the widest sand and the most upscale resorts; Station 2 in the middle is the busy hub around D'Mall, packed with restaurants and bars; and Station 3 in the south is quieter, with more reasonably priced places to stay. On the island's east side, Bulabog Beach turns into one of Asia's best kitesurfing spots during the northeast monsoon season of
November–April
Boracay once suffered badly from overdevelopment and sewage problems, and the government closed the entire island to tourists for six months, from
April 26, 2018
to
October 25

, for a major rehabilitation. Since then, unlicensed structures along the beachfront have been torn down, drinking, smoking, and fireworks on the beach have been restricted, and a system requiring a confirmed accredited accommodation booking to enter the island has been put in place. As a result, today's White Beach is far cleaner and better organized than before.
The island covers about 10 km², and according to the
census it has about 37,800 residents, spread across three barangays: Balabag, Manoc-Manoc, and Yapak. According to Malay Tourism Office figures, about 2.15 million visitors came in

, and the island's carrying capacity is set at about 19,215 people at a time. Boat lines and the beach are noticeably crowded over New Year and the Lunar New Year holiday, so book flights and accommodation early if you plan to visit then.

With direct flights from Korea to Kalibo and many operators offering Korean-language service, Boracay is especially well suited to first-time visitors to the Philippines, families with children, and honeymooning couples. Its biggest draw is being able to enjoy everything from water activities to spas, fine dining, and nightlife on a single island.
You sail off White Beach at sunset aboard a paraw, a traditional sailboat with bamboo outriggers on both sides. The sunset trip lasts about
30 minutes
and the daytime trip about
1 hour
, and most depart from in front of Station 1. A boat costs about
, varying with group size and the operator, and departures cluster around
for the sunset slot, so book ahead.

A half-day tour by bangka around Crystal Cove Island, Magic Island, a snorkeling spot (Crocodile Island), and Puka Shell Beach. Boats usually leave around
and return around
1–2 PM
, and the morning tour is recommended because the sea is calmer and the water is clearer. A join tour costs about
per person, and some packages leave out the Crystal Cove and Magic Island entrance fees (about
each), so check what's included.
A quiet beach at the island's northern tip, with more waves than White Beach and sand mixed with shell fragments. With fewer people around, it's a relaxed place to unwind.

During the

northeast monsoon season, lesson centers open one after another. A one-hour trial lesson costs about

3 hours

You can enjoy most water sports here, including helmet diving, parasailing, introductory scuba diving, and jet skiing. Helmet diving costs about
for
15 minutes
, and parasailing starts at about
per person. Always use an accredited operator.
A popular half-day tour with cliff diving, snorkeling, and a barbecue at the coastal cliffs on the Buruanga side of the Panay mainland, across from Boracay. It costs about
per person, including the round-trip boat plus lunch and drinks, and the jumping platforms range from low ones up to about

items.title: Rainy-day itinerary
items.subtitle: A day to enjoy even in Habagat season or on rainy days

children.text: Once D'Mall opens, browse the cafés and souvenir shops. In the rainy season, mornings often stay clear for an hour or two before clouding over in the afternoon, so keep outdoor plans for the morning.
Pick out shrimp and crab at D'Talipapa market and have them cooked paluto-style for lunch.
Relax with a spa or massage (about
for an hour) or spend the time at your accommodation's pool.
When the rain stops, head to Bulabog Beach and stroll until sunset, taking in the sea, which stays relatively calm even in the rainy season.
Wrap up the day at a live music bar at Station 2.
It's about
1 hour
from Manila to Caticlan Airport (MPH, Godofredo P. Ramos Airport), with daily flights on Philippine Airlines, Cebu Pacific, and others. From the airport to Caticlan Jetty Port is about
5 minutes
by tricycle.
Kalibo International Airport (KLO) is about
68km
by road from Caticlan Jetty Port, and Cebu Pacific and AirAsia fly there from Manila. Scheduled direct flights from Incheon arrive at this airport.
Incheon–Kalibo is operated by T'way Air (renamed Trinity Airways), with a flight time of about
4 hours 30 minutes
. From
to
October 24
it flies daily, departing Incheon at
and arriving in Kalibo at
; the return flight leaves Kalibo at
and arrives in Incheon at
From
June 8, 2026
to
July 13
, flights were reduced to four a week (Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun), and the schedule after
October 25
changes with each season, so check the airline's notices before booking. Royal Air Philippines suspended its Incheon–Caticlan route in
January 2026
, and whether it will resume has not been confirmed.
There are also direct flights to Caticlan from Clark on Cebu Pacific, AirAsia, and Sunlight Air, two to three times a day, taking about
1 hour 15 minutes
. This is convenient if you're departing from northern Manila or Angeles.
Flights to Caticlan and Kalibo are also available from Cebu.
From Kalibo Airport to Caticlan Jetty Port takes about
1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours
by van or bus and costs about
per person. A shared transfer booked in advance all the way to your accommodation costs about
per person, depending on the operator.
Boats from Caticlan Jetty Port also run at night, but between
and
they sometimes wait until they fill up with passengers, so a late arrival takes longer.
From Caticlan Jetty Port to Boracay's Cagban Port takes about
15 minutes
by bangka, costing around
per person, plus separate terminal and environmental fees.
During the southwest monsoon season (
June–October
), boats sometimes dock at Tambisaan Port on the island's east side to avoid rough waves.
It's convenient to book a bundled transfer package covering airport pickup, the boat crossing, and island transport (about
per person).
You can pay the island entry fee in advance through
Boracay iPass
, the Aklan provincial government's online registration and payment system, and receive a QR code beforehand. Check the latest announcements.
Since
December 19, 2024
, the Aklan provincial government has run Boracay iPass, an integrated ticketing system for paying the port fee, environmental fee, and boat fare in one go. The fees are an environmental fee of
for foreigners (
for Filipinos), a terminal fee of
, and a boat fare of

Online advance registration is not mandatory, so you can also pay at the port counter. Children aged 5 and under are exempt with proof of age; QR codes are non-refundable but can be transferred before they are scanned, and are valid until
December 31
of the year of application.
From Caticlan Airport to the jetty port, a tricycle to yourself costs about
, or about
per person if shared, and takes
7–10 minutes
. Including port registration, the boat, and getting to your accommodation, it usually takes
45–65 minutes
from the airport to your accommodation.
There are direct flights from Cebu (Mactan) to Caticlan taking about
1 hour 10 minutes
, operated by the Philippine Airlines group and Cebu Pacific. A one-way fare is about
, and seats fill up quickly in the peak season from
December
to
April
From Iloilo City to Caticlan it takes about
5–6 hours
by bus or van. If you're combining the trip with sightseeing in Iloilo City, traveling up overland is an option.
Electric tricycles (e-trikes) are the main way to get around the island. A shared ride costs about
per person, and a charter costs about
depending on distance.
Along White Beach, it's most convenient to walk along the beachfront path behind the sand.
Boracay's seasons are shaped by the wind. From
November
to
May
is the northeast monsoon (Amihan) season, when White Beach on the island's west side is sheltered from the wind, giving it calm water and the clearest sea.
December–February
is cool and pleasant and the most popular time to visit, while
March–May
sees almost no rain but is the peak of summer heat, with midday temperatures climbing to around 34°C.
From
June
to
October

is the southwest monsoon (Habagat) season, bringing frequent rain, higher waves on White Beach, and more days with seaweed washing ashore. On the plus side, Bulabog Beach calms down and accommodation prices drop significantly. Flights and boats can be canceled due to typhoons between
July–October
. In the third week of
January

, nearby Kalibo hosts the Ati-Atihan Festival, one of the Philippines' biggest celebrations. Rooms sell out early during Korean Lunar New Year and Chuseok holidays, as well as during Holy Week in the Philippines.
Typhoons can pass through even in the dry season. In
November 2025

, Typhoon Tino (international name Kalmaegi) and Typhoon Uwan halted boats between Caticlan and Boracay and water activities, and some flights to Caticlan from Manila and Cebu were canceled. If you're departing in
November
December
, choose flights and accommodation that can be changed, and leave at least a day of slack for your flight home.

items.label: Accommodation
items.note: Only accredited accommodation may be used

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
In Boracay, only accommodations accredited by the Department of Tourism (DOT) may be used, and you'll be asked for proof of booking on arrival. Station 1 has upscale resorts from
a night and up; Station 2 offers mid-range hotels (
) with easy access to transport and restaurants; and Station 3 and the area behind the beach have more reasonably priced rooms in the
range. The large resort complexes on the island's north side are quiet, have private beaches, and are popular with families.

The food scene here is extremely varied. Buying shrimp, crab, and lobster at D'Talipapa market and having a nearby restaurant cook it for you — known as paluto — is a Boracay classic. Jonah's Fruit Shake's mango shake, a fixture since the

, and the calamansi muffin at Real Coffee & Tea Café have long been considered must-tries in Boracay. Several Korean restaurants are also on the island, so even picky family travelers have little to worry about.
You have options beyond the beachfront. The Bulabog Beach side draws kitesurfers during the windy
November–April

season and tends to have lower room rates than White Beach, while Diniwid Beach and the Puka Shell Beach area in the north of the island are quiet. When booking, check whether the property is on the Department of Tourism's accredited list, how far it is from the beach, and how much noise there is from the Station 2 bar strip. D'Mall usually opens around
and stays open until
(until 2:00 AM on Fridays and Saturdays), and some small shops accept cash only.
Before arriving, prepare your accommodation booking confirmation (printed or on your phone) along with your passport. Entry can be delayed if your booking can't be confirmed.
There are several ATMs on the island, but they can run out of cash or have long lines during peak season, so bring some cash with you before you arrive.
The best spot to watch the sunset on White Beach is around Willy's Rock at Station 1. Stake out a spot before
Book water activities through your accommodation or an accredited operator rather than a beach tout, and always confirm exactly what's included in the price.
If you land at Kalibo Airport late at night, add the
1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours
road trip between Kalibo and Caticlan to the wait for a boat at the jetty port, and stay a night in Kalibo if needed.
During
November–April
, Bulabog Beach's strong winds make it better for watching kitesurfing than swimming — swim at White Beach instead.
If traveling with children, choose accommodation in a quieter section such as northern Station 1 or Station 3.
The environmental fee is charged once per stay, but the
terminal fee is also charged when you leave the island, so keep some cash for your last day.
Many small shops and street stalls accept cash only, and many places that take cards or e-wallets like GCash do so only for purchases of
or more. ATMs (BPI, BDO, Metrobank) are around D'Mall and White Beach.
Puka Shell Beach is about
by e-trike from the Station 2 side, and there is no entrance fee. It's hard to find a ride back, so ask the driver to wait or agree on a round-trip fare first.
Smoking, drinking, littering, and building sandcastles are banned or restricted on White Beach, with fines for violations. Smoke only in designated areas.
Settle on a price up front for any activity, massage, or currency exchange offered by a beach tout, and avoid unlicensed operators. Exchange money at a bank or an authorized money changer.
Jellyfish appear at certain times of year, so check the beach safety flags and notices, and if stung, rinse with vinegar and seek medical attention.
Direct midday sun is very strong. Use reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral, and drink water frequently.
Environmental fees, terminal fees, and entry procedures can change under local government ordinances. Check the latest notice before you travel.

If the coast guard halts boat service because of a typhoon or strong winds, getting between Caticlan and Boracay can be delayed by a day or more, so book your flight home at least a day after the day you leave the island.
The whole island of Boracay operates under strict environmental rules. Keep in mind that "surely this is fine here" thinking can lead to a hefty fine.
